Bayesian Mixed Models with ASReml Syntax

Source: R/flexybayes.R
flexybayes.Rd

Specify mixed models using ASReml formula syntax and estimate them on one of two active engines: INLA (integrated nested Laplace approximation) or brms (the Stan passthrough). Returns a three-part result: a GLM-compatible object for use with standard R packages (emmeans, marginaleffects, etc.), the native backend object for engine-specific diagnostics, and extras for secondary analyses.

Usage

flexybayes(
  fixed,
  random = NULL,
  residual = NULL,
  data,
  family = "gaussian",
  link = NULL,
  known_matrices = list(),
  weights = NULL,
  na_action = c("augment", "omit", "fail"),
  n_samples = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  chains = 4,
  seed = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  prior = NULL,
  prior_fixed_sd = 100,
  prior_vc_sd = 1,
  verbose = TRUE,
  mcmc_verbose = TRUE,
  return_code = FALSE,
  review_code = FALSE,
  backend = c("auto", "inla", "brms"),
  aggregate = "auto",
  plan = FALSE,
  syntax = c("auto", "asreml", "brms"),
  known_variance = NULL,
  fixed_alias = c("refuse", "drop"),
  rcov
)

fb(
  fixed,
  random = NULL,
  residual = NULL,
  data,
  family = "gaussian",
  link = NULL,
  known_matrices = list(),
  weights = NULL,
  na_action = c("augment", "omit", "fail"),
  n_samples = 1000,
  warmup = 500,
  chains = 4,
  seed = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  prior = NULL,
  prior_fixed_sd = 100,
  prior_vc_sd = 1,
  verbose = TRUE,
  mcmc_verbose = TRUE,
  return_code = FALSE,
  review_code = FALSE,
  backend = c("auto", "inla", "brms"),
  aggregate = "auto",
  plan = FALSE,
  syntax = c("auto", "asreml", "brms"),
  known_variance = NULL,
  fixed_alias = c("refuse", "drop"),
  rcov
)

Arguments

fixed

Two-sided formula response ~ fixed_effects. This is the universal entry's model slot: it accepts the ASReml fixed form (paired with random / residual) or a brms / lme4-style bar-grouped formula such as response ~ x + (1 | g) (in which case the grouping lives in the formula and random / residual must be left NULL). The grammar is detected from the call shape. Use syntax to force it.

Offsets. offset() terms in the fixed formula enter the linear predictor with a fixed coefficient of one on both engines, and several add. Each is evaluated against data and has to be a finite number on every row (fixed_offset_invalid otherwise). brms receives the terms in its formula; INLA receives the evaluated offset through inla()'s offset argument, and a Gaussian identity-link fit reads its centre, scale and default priors from the response minus the offset. The aggregated route carries an offset exactly on the Gaussian family (subtracted before the cell statistics are taken) and the Poisson family (as exposure), and refuses one on the binomial family (fixed_offset_unsupported), where aggregate = "auto" takes the per-row route. predict() on new data evaluates the offset there and refuses when a column it reads is absent (newdata_offset_missing). An offset() in random or residual is refused.

random

One-sided formula: ~ random_terms using ASReml syntax. "Parsed" and "fitted" are not the same claim, so the term catalogue is two lists.

Parsed and fitted (emitted by at least one active engine): vm(), at(), diag(), idh(), us(), ar1(), spl(), ped(), dsum(), id(), and nested colon terms, including the per-trial separable AR1 field described under "Spatial and temporal autoregressive fields" below.

Parsed and refused by name. fa(f, k):g, the factor-analytic genotype-by-environment covariance, is refused on both engines (factor_analytic_not_repeatable). On simulated trials with a known covariance, the genetic-correlation intervals of INLA fits covered the true value less often than required (134 and 125 of 150 for k = 1 and 2, against 136), and flexyBayes has no factor-analytic lowering for brms. Write diag(f):g, which fits on both engines, or us(f):g on brms. The bare spelling fa(v, k), with no grouping factor for the covariance to apply to, keeps its own refusal (fa_not_representable). corh(f):g is likewise ASReml syntax that flexyBayes parses and refuses by name. It is described just below.

Heterogeneous variances. diag(f):g, idh(f):g and at(f):g all fit one variance per level of f with no covariance between levels: the usual multi-environment structure, where the genotype variance differs by site. ASReml treats diag() and idh() as the same structure, and so does flexyBayes. The three spellings emit identical code. us(f):g estimates every pairwise correlation instead, at k(k+1)/2 parameters against diag()'s k.

corh(f):g, heterogeneous variances with a single shared correlation, is refused on both engines: flexyBayes has no lowering for it, and approximating it with either neighbour would change the parameter count. With one variance for every level and a correlation of zero or more, random = ~ g + f:g is the same covariance and fits on both engines.

Selected levels. at(f, level):g gives the random effect g only to the rows where f takes one of the named levels, with one variance per named level, as in ASReml. at(design, "split"):mainplot is a main-plot effect in the split-plot trials alone. Levels are written as values, at(f, c("a", "b")), or as positions in levels(f), at(f, 2). A level the data do not have is refused (at_level_not_in_data). It fits on both engines and reports sd_<g>__<f><level>, the name at(f):g gives the same level.

diag(f):g fits on both engines. us(f):g fits on brms, and INLA refuses it, so auto routes such a model to brms.

Spatial and temporal autoregressive fields. ar1(t) and the separable ar1(row):ar1(col) are written here, on the random side, and emitted on INLA as a latent autoregressive field plus the Gaussian observation nugget. Four hyperparameters on a field grid: the row correlation, the column correlation, the field SD and the nugget SD, all four printed by summary(). Each correlation is named after the factor it runs along, rho_<factor>: rho_row and rho_col for ar1(row):ar1(col), and the same two names for ar1(col):ar1(row). The field is faithful only with one observation per grid node, so an incomplete or replicated grid refuses (keep the unobserved nodes as design cells with the default na_action = "augment"). flexyBayes has no brms lowering for the field, so brms refuses.

That four-parameter model is not ASReml's separable residual, which is one correlated residual with no independent plot error: three parameters, nested inside this one as the nugget goes to zero. On data with real plot-to-plot noise the two return different correlations, because a nugget-free model must absorb independent noise into the correlated structure and is pulled towards zero by it. The gap grows with the share of the total variance the nugget holds, and it falls on the correlations a reader acts on. Neither model is wrong. The residual form is written on the residual side, residual = ~ ar1(row):ar1(col), described under residual below.

Per-trial nested field. id(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits one separable AR1 field per level of trial on INLA, via the replicate = mechanism: one complete grid per trial, each with its own realised field. The row correlation, column correlation and field SD are shared across every level of trial, not estimated per trial. This is the model ASReml fits under the same spelling.

A field for each trial. at(trial):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits a separate field on each trial, with its own SD and correlations, as ASReml does: three parameters per trial, reported as sd_spatial__trial<level>, rho_row__trial<level> and rho_col__trial<level> for ar1(row):ar1(col), plus the shared Gaussian nugget. at(trial, level):ar1(row):ar1(col) fits the field on the named trials only. Each trial's plots must fill its own grid. brms refuses both.

Units followed through time. ar1(t):g, or the same term written g:ar1(t), fits one AR1 series along t within each level of g, independent across levels, with one correlation and one field SD shared by every level and the Gaussian nugget on top, three hyperparameters in all. This is the units-by-occasions repeated-measures covariance of Verbyla and Cullis (1992) written on the random side: g indexes the plots, animals or series and t the occasions, whose levels must be in time order. An occasion a unit missed stays as a design row with the response NA under the default na_action = "augment", and the t by g grid must be complete in that sense, one row per node. brms refuses, as for the other fields.

residual

One-sided formula: ~ residual_structure. Default ~ units (iid residuals). ~ dsum(~ units | env), and the equivalent ~ at(env):units, give a separate residual variance per level of env. Only families that carry a residual scale parameter can have one made heterogeneous. A Poisson's dispersion is a function of its mean, so there is nothing there to vary, and the request is refused.

~ ar1(row):ar1(col) is ASReml's separable residual: one correlated residual with no nugget, three parameters (sd_spatial, rho_row, rho_col), and no sigma row. ~ dsum(~ ar1(row):ar1(col) | trial) fits it separately in each trial, with names suffixed __trial<level>. Both fit on INLA for a Gaussian response with the identity link and one plot per grid cell, where the observation error is fixed at a variance of exp(-12) on the standardised response; brms refuses them. They cannot be combined with a random-side field. ~ ar1(t) and ~ ar1(row):col are refused on both engines, with a pointer to the random-side field described under random above.

data

A data.frame containing all variables referenced in the formulas.

family

Character: "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson", "negative_binomial", "gamma", "beta", "hurdle_gamma" or "lognormal". The last two are brms only: INLA's likelihood roster has no hurdle gamma, and no INLA lognormal fit is validated, so the family gate refuses both there and backend = "auto" routes them to brms. A family object (binomial(), gaussian(), brms::lognormal()) is also accepted, goes through the same gate as its name, and supplies its own link, so Gamma() means the inverse link it names, not the log link family = "gamma" defaults to. Passing a family object together with a contradicting link is refused, not resolved. A family outside this set is refused at the door. Where the boundary is flexyBayes's own and not the engines', the refusal says so and inst/KNOWN_ISSUES.md records it. A response outside the family's domain (0 or negative for "gamma" or "lognormal", negative for "hurdle_gamma", at or outside [0, 1] for "beta") is refused by name (family_response_domain_violation) before any engine runs. A missing (NA) response is na_action's concern, not a domain violation.

link

Character or NULL: override the default link function (e.g., "probit" for binomial). Leave it unset when family is a family object, which carries its own link. The links fitted, default first: gaussian identity, log, inverse, logit, probit, cloglog, cauchit; binomial logit, probit, probit_approx, cloglog, cauchit, softit, identity, log; poisson log, identity, sqrt; negative_binomial log, identity, sqrt, softplus, squareplus; gamma log, identity, inverse; hurdle_gamma log, identity, inverse, softplus, squareplus; beta logit; lognormal identity. backend = "inla" takes the default link only, refusing any other by name (inla_gate_refused), and backend = "auto" fits another link on brms. A link outside the list is refused by name (unsupported_family) on every backend.

known_matrices

Named list of matrices referred to in the random formula (e.g., list(Gmat = G_mat, Amat = A_mat)). The carrier is declared with the fb_cov() constructor inside the random term: a dense covariance (vm(group, cov = fb_cov(G, type = "dense")); brms), a user-supplied lower-triangular Cholesky factor (vm(group, cov = fb_cov(L, type = "chol")); brms), or a sparse precision matrix Matrix::dgCMatrix (vm(group, cov = fb_cov(Q, type = "precision")); INLA and brms). INLA takes the precision and pedigree-precision carriers only, and refuses by name a dense or Cholesky carrier, pointing at solve(V) or at brms, and a block carrier, which INLA would fit with one standard deviation per block, pointing at the precision carrier of the block-diagonal inverse. The bare dense forms vm(group, V = ...) / ped(group, A = ...) remain the default. The legacy v0.3.7 keyword carriers (chol = , precision = , blocks = , low_rank_factor = ) are deprecated and emit a migration warning. See the formula-surface vignette for per-type worked examples.

weights

Optional numeric weight vector (length N). Lowered for family = "gaussian" with the identity link only, in the ASReml / lme4 / glm(weights=) precision sense, Var(y_i) = sigma^2 / w_i: INLA's scale = w per-observation precision multiplier, and on brms a known offset on the log-link sigma distributional parameter (not brms's own weights() addition term, which implements a different, likelihood-power quantity). A constant vector (including rep(1, N)) is the unweighted model under a different spelling and passes through unchanged. A non-constant vector on any other family, or a non-identity link on Gaussian, is refused by name (weights_requires_gaussian) instead of silently producing the unweighted posterior. Likelihood-power, frequency, trials and exposure are different models and cannot share this argument silently. aggregate = TRUE together with weights is also refused by name (weights_not_aggregatable): the aggregated route's closed-form sufficient statistics do not carry a per-observation weight through the compression.

na_action

How to treat observations whose response is missing, and, through the list form below, observations whose predictors are missing.

"augment" (default) retains missing-response rows, carrying the missing response as a latent quantity the engine marginalises, and completes the design grid where the absent cells are determinable. This is ASReml's na.method(y = "include") behaviour, and it matters whenever the model carries a covariance indexed by the design: deleting the row of a lost plot changes the index set a separable AR1 field is built over, so the fitted model is no longer the model that was written down. "omit" drops the rows (complete-case), and a structured covariance over the resulting broken grid then refuses downstream. "fail" refuses if any response is missing, and leaves the design grid alone.

A response value that is NaN or infinite, as log(0) gives, is not a missing observation. It refuses by name under every setting (response_not_finite). Set it to NA to treat it as missing.

The argument also accepts the object an ASReml user already writes, asreml::na.method(y = , x = ), and the bare list of the same shape for readers without an asreml licence:

flexybayes(..., na_action = list(y = "include", x = "fail"))

The response words map include to "augment", omit to "omit", fail to "fail". The covariate words are ASReml's own. x = "fail" (the default, and ASReml's) refuses a missing predictor. x = "omit" drops the affected rows with a warning naming the count and the columns. x = "include", ASReml's zero-fill (Reference Manual 4.2, section 3.11), is refused by name, because a zero is a value the plot did not have. A value arriving as an unreduced na.method() default vector is read as its first element, which is the policy ASReml itself would use.

Under ignorability, and only when both representations put the same prior on the same model parameters, the posterior for those parameters is the same whether a missing response is augmented or omitted – augmentation preserves the representation, not information. A backend default prior can depend on the realised design matrix, so it does not establish that common-prior condition automatically. The identity is a statement about the posterior and not a promise about what an optimiser returns: the two settings hand the engine an intact design and a ragged one, and on a weakly identified mode they can land in different places. Where missingness depends on the unobserved response itself, both are biased and neither this argument nor any diagnostic here will tell you so.

n_samples

Integer: number of posterior samples per chain.

warmup

Integer: number of warmup (burn-in) iterations per chain.

chains

Integer: number of MCMC chains.

seed

Integer or NULL: the seed for the sampler, on the engine that samples.

On brms it is forwarded to brms::brm(seed = ) and fixes Stan's draws: two fits of the same model to the same data under the same seed, chains and backend return identical draws. With NULL (the default) brms passes no seed and Stan runs with one drawn for it. On the cmdstanr backend that draw comes from R's random-number stream, so it follows set.seed() only when nothing else draws from the stream first. Either way the seed Stan ran with is kept at fit$extras$reproducibility$seed$as_run, and a refit under that value returns the same draws. Draws taken later from the fitted object, such as brms::posterior_epred() on new levels, follow R's random-number stream and not this seed.

On INLA the seed has no effect: INLA::inla() takes no seed, and the argument says once that it was not used. A refit in a fresh R session can reach a different mode whatever the seed (see the section INLA threads). The thread setting an INLA fit ran with is recorded beside the engine versions, in the same record.

control

A named list of sampler control settings or NULL, forwarded to brms::brm(control = ). This is the route to adapt_delta and max_treedepth: control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95) is the standard first response to divergent transitions. NULL (the default) uses brms's own settings. A no-op on the INLA path, as seed is.

prior

An optional fb_prior() object specifying priors via the PC-canonical hybrid DSL (preferred). When supplied it overrides prior_vc_sd for the variance components it covers. See fb_prior(). On INLA, a random-effect standard deviation the prior does not name takes the package's default, half_normal(scale = s) with the family-aware s described under prior_vc_sd (divided by the covariate's standard deviation for an uncorrelated slope); prior_summary() lists what was filled. A standard deviation the prior does name is left exactly as written.

prior_fixed_sd

Numeric: SD for fixed-effect normal priors, applied uniformly to the intercept, factor contrasts, continuous slopes, factor x continuous interactions, and I()-expression terms. Default 100: weakly informative on the natural response scale for the vast majority of agricultural / clinical responses (covers responses with central tendency up to several hundred without crushing the posterior toward zero), while still regularising at sample sizes below ~ 30 per coefficient. Set wider (e.g. 1000) for responses on a larger natural scale, or narrower for explicit shrinkage. A weakly-informative normal prior on the data scale, in the spirit of the weakly-informative-prior literature for regression coefficients (e.g. Gelman et al. 2008, Annals of Applied Statistics 2(4):1360-1383). Applied when you supply it, on every backend: brms receives one normal(0, sd) row per fixed-effect class, and INLA receives control.fixed with prec = 1 / sd^2 on the slopes and the intercept alike. Left unsupplied, brms keeps its own fixed-effect default (flat coefficients and a response-centred student_t intercept), because replacing a response-centred intercept prior with normal(0, 100) is a different model for any response far from zero. INLA gives each column built from a numeric variable the covariate-scaled default normal(0, 1e5 * sd(y) / sd(x)) on an identity link and normal(0, sqrt(1000) / sd(x)) on a log or logit link, with sd(x) read over the rows whose response is observed, so a covariate's units do not change the fit, and keeps its own prec = 0.001 on factor contrasts and its flat intercept. prior_summary() names what a fit ran under. A supplied value is never rescaled by a covariate: it is a standard deviation in response units per covariate unit, so on a covariate recorded in small units (a large coefficient) it can bind. Measure the covariate in natural units, or leave the argument unsupplied on INLA.

prior_vc_sd

Numeric: hyperparameter for the legacy lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) variance-component prior. Note: when both prior and prior_vc_sd are left at their defaults, the package applies a half-normal default on the SD scale (half_normal(scale = s) with family-aware s: 5 * sd(y) for Gaussian, 5 on the logit scale for binomial / beta, 3 on the log scale for Poisson / negative-binomial / gamma) to sigma and every named random-effect group, on both engines, with the scale on the standard deviation of an uncorrelated random slope divided by the standard deviation of its numeric covariate. It is weakly informative and has no upper bound. A half-t or half-Cauchy (Gelman 2006, Bayesian Analysis 1(3):515-534) is stated through fb_prior(). Before 0.13.0 the default was uniform(0, U) with U equal to the scale above. The legacy lognormal(0, 1) default fires only when prior_vc_sd is passed explicitly. Silence the one-time announcement message via options(flexyBayes.silence_default_prior_note = TRUE). When it is passed explicitly it reaches both active engines as the same density on the standard-deviation scale: brms as a lognormal(0, prior_vc_sd) prior row, INLA as the expression prior that writes that density in INLA's log-precision parameterisation. The two engines therefore carry the same variance-component prior.

verbose

Logical: print the generated backend code to the console.

mcmc_verbose

Logical: show the sampler's progress bar. Has no effect on INLA, which does not sample.

return_code

Logical: if TRUE, return the generated backend code without fitting the model: the Stan program on backend = "brms", the INLA formula, family and hyperparameter list on backend = "inla".

review_code

Logical: if TRUE, do not fit the model immediately; instead return a <flexybayes_review> deferred-execution object carrying the generated Stan code, the resolved prior, the parsed intermediate representation (IR), the captured call, and a snapshot of .Random.seed. Inspect the code with cat_code() and run the deferred fit with proceed(). A second proceed() call returns the cached fit. Useful as a teaching / auditing surface before a long MCMC run. Default FALSE preserves the existing run-immediately semantics. A session-level override is available via options(flexyBayes.review_code_default = TRUE). The argument value at call time always wins. Closest published precedent: brms::stancode() plus the chains = 0 idiom for "do everything except sampling". review_code = TRUE and return_code = TRUE are mutually exclusive. brms is the only engine with a code slot, so review_code = TRUE is available under backend = "brms" and under "auto" (which resolves the code modes to brms). Under backend = "inla" it refuses with review_code_backend_unsupported: the deferred-execution token would need an INLA-side code slot, which is queued for a later release.

backend

Character: one of "auto" (default), "inla", or "brms". INLA fits the latent-Gaussian model class by nested Laplace approximation, without sampling. brms is the Stan passthrough. Any other value, including a formerly-registered engine name this package withdrew entirely (see NEWS.md), refuses with unknown_backend naming the two active engines.

What "auto" does. The call runs lgm_gate() and routes to INLA when the model is latent-Gaussian feasible and INLA is installed. Otherwise it routes to brms when brms is installed and its capability predicate accepts the model. When neither can represent the model, the call refuses with auto_no_active_route instead of fitting something else. Nothing is translated silently. auto does change engine in one case after starting: an INLA program failure is caught and re-routed to brms, and a message reports it. The fit's class and backend field always record which engine produced it. backend_decision() surfaces the full dispatch trace (including rejected_routes) post-fit, and fb_backend_status() reports which engines are usable. The one-time notes on the auto path are silenceable via options(flexyBayes.silence_auto_fallback_note = TRUE) (gate refusal or an INLA numerical failure) and options(flexyBayes.silence_auto_inla_missing_note = TRUE) (INLA not installed).

What each engine represents. INLA fits: Gaussian LMM, simple random intercept; GLMM (binomial, Poisson, negative binomial, gamma, beta), simple random effect; Uncorrelated random slope; Factor-by-numeric fixed interaction; Nested / interaction random effects, multi-stratum; Heterogeneous variance by factor level; Heterogeneous residual by factor level; Baseline heteroscedastic MET: iid genotype, iid genotype-by-environment and a sectioned residual; Known-covariance genomic / pedigree random effect; Separable AR1 spatial field; Per-trial separable AR1 field; Grouped temporal AR1 field; Univariate P-spline; Observation weights (Gaussian, identity link); Exact sufficient-statistic aggregation (binomial, Poisson). INLA refuses: Hurdle gamma (zero mass plus a positive gamma part); Correlated random slope; Unstructured genotype-by-environment covariance; Heterogeneous variances with one shared correlation; Factor-analytic genotype-by-environment covariance; Multi-trait covariance; Exact sufficient-statistic aggregation (Gaussian). brms fits: Gaussian LMM, simple random intercept; GLMM (binomial, Poisson, negative binomial, gamma, beta), simple random effect; Hurdle gamma (zero mass plus a positive gamma part); Uncorrelated random slope; Factor-by-numeric fixed interaction; Correlated random slope; Nested / interaction random effects, multi-stratum; Heterogeneous variance by factor level; Unstructured genotype-by-environment covariance; Heterogeneous residual by factor level; Baseline heteroscedastic MET: iid genotype, iid genotype-by-environment and a sectioned residual; Known-covariance genomic / pedigree random effect; Observation weights (Gaussian, identity link). brms refuses: Heterogeneous variances with one shared correlation; Factor-analytic genotype-by-environment covariance; Multi-trait covariance; Separable AR1 spatial field; Per-trial separable AR1 field; Grouped temporal AR1 field; Univariate P-spline. The per-class table is in README.md, and with a note on each row in system.file("KNOWN_ISSUES.md", package = "flexyBayes").

Caution (small-group random effects). Both engines apply the same default prior, the half-normal on each standard deviation, which the INLA path represents exactly as an expression prior on the log-precision, so they agree on the variance component far more closely than in earlier versions. A model with very few groups nonetheless carries a weakly-identified variance component (the data say little about the between-group spread), and INLA's Laplace approximation is less accurate there than full MCMC. For a flagship random-intercept model with few groups, pin backend = "brms" or supply an explicit informative prior (a half-Cauchy, per Gelman 2006, as in the priors and regularisation vignette).

Convergence. The brms fit emits a warning when the sampler may not have converged (a parameter with Rhat at or above 1.1, or a low effective sample size). Treat such a posterior with caution: increase warmup / n_samples, simplify the model, or supply a more informative prior, and inspect the full diagnostics with summary(). Silence the warning (for intentionally short fits) via options(flexyBayes.silence_convergence_warning = TRUE). An INLA fit does not sample and carries no such warning.

Code inspection. brms is the only engine with a code slot, so return_code = TRUE / review_code = TRUE under "auto" resolve to brms, but only when brms can represent the model. Where it cannot, the call refuses with auto_no_active_route instead of returning the code for a different model. backend = "inla" with return_code = TRUE returns the INLA formula, family and hyperparameter list. With review_code = TRUE it refuses until the INLA-side code slot lands.

aggregate

One of "auto" (default), TRUE, or FALSE. Exact sufficient-statistics aggregation gate. INLA is the only engine with an aggregated emit. "auto" consults the aggregation plan and routes a binomial-logit or poisson-log model through the per-cell path when the IR is in scope (fixed plus random intercept; productive compression) and the model reaches INLA. A Gaussian model is fitted per row: the aggregated Gaussian route cannot yet carry the residual prior, so TRUE on a Gaussian model refuses by name (aggregation_residual_prior_not_composed). TRUE also raises a structured refusal when the plan declares ineligibility, or when no active engine offers an aggregated route. FALSE skips the gate entirely. Aggregated fits carry $exactness == "aggregated_exact", the dispatch trace's path slot reads "aggregated_count", and their summary reports no marginal likelihood (aggregated_evidence_unavailable). For out-of-core datasets that do not fit in memory, see flexybayes_stream().

plan

Logical: if TRUE, short-circuit after intermediate representation (IR) build and return a <fb_plan> object carrying the IR, the routing decision, the representation plan, the aggregation plan, and the prediction plan, without emitting backend code or fitting. Equivalent to calling fb_plan() with the same formula triple, exposed inline as flexybayes(plan = TRUE) so users can reach the planning object without re-typing the call. Default FALSE preserves the run- immediately semantics. Mutually exclusive with return_code and review_code.

syntax

One of "auto" (default), "asreml", or "brms". Selects how fixed is interpreted. "auto" detects the grammar from the call shape (a bar-grouped formula is read as brms, otherwise ASReml). The other values force a grammar.

known_variance

Optional numeric vector of length N, or an N x N covariance matrix (below). A vector is a known variance for each response, added to the estimated residual variance, Var(y_i) = sigma^2 + v_i. This is the second stage of a two-stage analysis, where each response is a first-stage estimate (a variety mean in one trial, say) and v_i is the variance of that estimate. weights is a different model, Var(y_i) = sigma^2 / w_i. Given both, the residual variance is sigma^2 / w_i + v_i. Lowered for family = "gaussian" with the identity link: brms fits y | se(sqrt(v), sigma = TRUE), and INLA a row effect with known variance v_i. The summaries report sigma as the estimated part, and fitted values on both engines leave the known part out. A vector of zeros fits the model without it. Any other family refuses with known_variance_not_supported, and a vector that is not one finite, non-negative value per row with known_variance_invalid. A symmetric positive-definite N x N matrix K is a known covariance, Var(y) = sigma^2 I + K, as when the first stage returns the full covariance of its estimates. It is fitted on INLA as a latent effect with precision K^-1. brms has no term for it and refuses with known_variance_not_supported. A row and column of zeros marks a row without a known part. A matrix that is not square, symmetric and positive definite over the rows of data refuses with known_variance_invalid.

fixed_alias

"refuse" (the default) or "drop": what to do with a fixed-effect column that is a linear combination of the columns before it on the rows with a response, as in a factorial with empty cells. INLA and brms would report such a column at its prior, so by default the fit refuses with fixed_effects_aliased and names the columns. "drop" drops them as asreml 4.2 does, on INLA: terms are taken in model order, and within a term by descending factor levels, the term's first factor varying slowest. A column that is a linear combination of the columns before it is fixed at zero. summary() reports it with estimate 0 and no standard error, the columns are listed in fit$extras$fixed_alias$dropped, and a prediction whose row is not a combination of the fitting rows is NA with status "Aliased" (see predict.flexybayes_inla()).

rcov

Defunct in flexyBayes 0.9.0. This was the ASReml 3 name for the residual-structure argument. ASReml 4 renamed it to residual, and flexyBayes follows the ASReml 4 name. Supplying rcov now raises an error. Use residual instead.

Value

An object of class "flexybayes", a list with three components.

$glm

A GLM-compatible object (class c("flexybayes_glm", "glm", "lm")) with posterior mean coefficients, vcov, residuals, fitted values, etc. Works with summary(), emmeans() and marginaleffects().

$brms or $inla

The native backend object: a live brmsfit on the brms path, or INLA's own fitted object on the INLA path. Use with bayesplot, posterior::as_draws(), and each engine's own accessors.

$extras

Additional outputs: posterior summary, convergence diagnostics, variance_comps, blups, predictions, generated code, param_names, parse_info, call_info, run_time, model_info, and reproducibility: the R, flexyBayes and engine versions, the thread settings and the seed the fit ran with, which print() shows.

If return_code = TRUE, returns the generated backend code instead: a character string holding the Stan program on the brms path, or a list of the formula, family and hyperparameter specification on the INLA path.

INLA threads

An INLA fit runs on one thread, num.threads = "1:1", whatever INLA::inla.setOption() holds. With more threads, identical calls can return different variance components where the data inform a variance only weakly. On a 48-trial barley model with 22 localities, eight identical fits at "4:1" gave the locality variance from 0.58 to 42.3, and at "1:1" from 0.75 to 0.79, with the fixed effects unchanged. Set options(flexyBayes.inla_threads = "4:1") for another plan, or "inla" for INLA's own default. The plan a fit ran with is in $extras$reproducibility.

One thread does not guarantee the same result in a new R session. Identical calls in fresh R processes can reach different modes. On a 48-trial barley series, four processes reached two modes, 0.10 apart in log marginal likelihood, whose variance component standard deviations differed by at most 3.4%. On six trials of the same series, the modes differed by up to 26%.

Each INLA fit is therefore run three times: once in this session and twice in fresh R processes started through callr. The fit with the highest log marginal likelihood is returned (the first of equal ones). options(flexyBayes.inla_best_of = k) sets the number of fits, a whole number of one or more; 1 fits once in this session, as 0.16.0 did, and any other value refuses with inla_best_of_invalid. Above 1 without callr installed, the fit refuses with isolation_requires_callr. A fit that fails in a separate process stops the call with that process's message. $extras$reproducibility$best_of holds each fit's log marginal likelihood and mode status, the fit kept, the range of the marginal likelihoods, and each standard deviation per fit with its largest difference across the fits, relative to the smallest. print() and summary() add a line when a standard deviation differs by more than 5%. The restart probe of the numerical-confirm gate examines the fit kept. The fresh-process fits run beside the session fit, at most options(flexyBayes.inla_best_of_workers) fits at once (default: all of them) and fewer, with a message, when the free memory holds fewer. The record gives each fit's time in seconds (wall_s) and whether they ran at once (parallel).

Fitting in a separate process

options(flexyBayes.isolation = "process") runs the engine fit in a separate R process started through callr, which is in Suggests. Without callr the request refuses with isolation_requires_callr before anything is fitted. The option applies to flexybayes(), fb_brms(), fb_inla() and proceed(), and fb_isolated_lapply() runs any loop of calls the same way. The default, "none", fits in this session.

If the operating system kills that process, or compiled code crashes inside it, the call refuses with isolated_process_died, naming the engine, the function called, and the exit status or signal, and this session carries on. A failure inside the fit, a refusal for instance, arrives exactly as it would without the option. The call is not retried.

The separate process loads the flexyBayes code this session loaded and starts from this session's options, INLA settings, environment variables and random-number state, so it fits the same model with the same seed, and the random-number stream moves on as it would have. Messages, warnings and printed output come back in the order they were raised, and the fit records the process in $extras$isolation. A brms fit with a seed returns the same draws either way. INLA does not return identical numbers for two identical calls in one session, and an isolated INLA fit agrees with an in-process one as closely as two in-process fits agree. The separate process starts with an empty global environment, so the formula finds its variables in data. Starting the process and moving the data and the fit costs time on every call.

Deprecated

fb() is deprecated in flexyBayes 0.13.0 and will be removed in a later release. Call flexybayes(), which takes the same arguments. A call to fb() warns with a condition of class flexybayes_deprecated.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# live fit, needs an active backend (INLA or brms/Stan)
data(met_example, package = "flexyBayes")
# Simple random intercept model (small budget for example purposes)
fit <- flexybayes(
  fixed  = yield ~ env,
  random = ~ geno,
  data   = met_example$dat,
  n_samples = 100, warmup = 100, chains = 1, verbose = FALSE
)
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
} # }
